cracks.prompt:
A texture for a game VFX artist: FRACTURE CRACKS, as when a thick sheet of dark glass is shattered by several blows. Only the cracks themselves are drawn, as lines of white and pale ice-blue light on pure black (#000000), seen straight from above, perfectly flat, with no perspective.

Five or six points of impact are spread over the whole picture. From each a web of cracks runs out: long main cracks, straight for a stretch and then turning at a sharp angle, that cross the whole picture and join the cracks of the other impacts; thinner cracks branching off them; fine hairline cracks between; and close round each point of impact a small dense spider's web of ring-shaped and radial cracks. The main cracks are bold, with a white-hot core and a thin soft glow; the hairlines are very fine. The cracks cover the picture evenly from edge to edge and run off all four edges.

Nothing else is in the picture: no surface, no glass texture, no reflections, no shards, no dust, no objects, no text.

lane-light.prompt:
A texture for a game VFX artist: a COLUMN OF LIGHT rising from the floor, as when one lane of a rhythm game's track lights up. Seen straight from the front, perfectly flat, with no perspective, on pure black (#000000).

At the very BOTTOM edge of the picture lies a bright, white-hot horizontal band of light that spans the picture's whole width. From it the light rises upward and fills the whole width of the picture, out to the left and right edges (a wide column, not a thin beam): it is made of many fine vertical streaks and rays of different lengths and brightness, softly glowing between them, with a few small bright motes drifting up among them. The light is brightest at the bottom and fades smoothly upward, and the top quarter of the picture is black.

White and grey light only, with no colour at all, because the game colours it itself. Nothing else is in the picture: no floor, no objects, no figures, no frame, no text.
